name: black midi
label: Rough Trade
lede: Four BRIT School students played their first gig at a Brixton pub before most of them were 18, made three albums in four years, and ended it through an Instagram Live chat box.

hero.by: black midi at Haldern Pop, August 2019. Photo: Martin Schumann, Wikimedia Commons

eras.title: Born at the Windmill
eras.text: Geordie Greep, Matt Kwasniewski-Kelvin, Morgan Simpson and Cameron Picton met at the BRIT School in London, where, Picton says, two years of free rehearsal time let them get the stupid stuff out early. A Brixton pub gave them a stage, a residency and a producer before they had a record out.

years.h: Greep and Kwasniewski-Kelvin bring in a prize-winning drummer
years.p: After separate jams at the BRIT School, the two guitarists recruit Simpson, the 2014 Young Drummer of the Year from a Jamaican musical family. Picton joins later on bass.

years.cap: Black midi on a festival stage
years.h: First gig: the Windmill in Brixton, opening for Leg Puppy
years.p: Some of the band aren't 18 yet. The pub gives them a residency, and they become one of the biggest names in what gets called the Windmill scene.
years.xp:
The Windmill's booker Tim Perry has said it plainly: "Black Midi were born here." The band paid it back later, playing fundraising livestreams when the pub was at risk during Covid.

Producer [[Dan Carey|41b34054-f491-4991-9495-477617fdc81a]] was in the room for the opening night of the residency and asked to record them soon after.

years.h: NTS posts a session filmed at Flesh and Bone studios
years.p: It's the first original black midi music anyone outside Brixton can hear. The song comes out a year later as the single "Talking Heads".

years.h: Can's Damo Suzuki fronts black midi at the Windmill
years.p: The night with Damo Suzuki, once the singer of Can, comes out on cassette in September as Damo Suzuki Live at the Windmill Brixton with 'Sound Carriers' black midi.

years.h: "bmbmbm" is the first single, on Dan Carey's Speedy Wunderground
years.p: One song, cut with Carey for his own label, the producer who'd seen them at the Windmill and wanted them in his studio.

yt: black midi, Full Performance (Live on KEXP), Iceland Airwaves 2018
years.h: A KEXP set in a Reykjavík hostel goes around the world
years.p: Five songs from an album nobody has heard, filmed at Kex Hostel during Iceland Airwaves. The clip spreads on YouTube and gives the band an audience far beyond London.
years.xp: At the time the band had one single out, so the live show was the only way to hear them. KEXP's writer: "Their riffs surged through the room like someone touching an electric fence and grabbing the hand of someone next to them."

years.cap: Black midi at KEX Hostel, Reykjavík, November 2018
q: If the album and the gig are just the same, it's a bit sad.
years.h: Five days in Carey's studio make most of an album
years.p: Eight of Schlagenheim's nine tracks are cut in five days, with piano, accordion, banjo and drum machines the band can't play live.
years.xp: That was the point. "The idea was to do stuff that's impossible to do live," Greep said. The non-album song "Sweater" comes from the same sessions.

eras.title: Rough Trade and a made-up word
eras.text: Rough Trade signed them in January 2019 and kept the mystery going by holding back even the track list. Schlagenheim made the Mercury shortlist; when the pandemic shut the stages, they read short stories over jams and played a charity gig for the pub that started them.

years.cap: SXSW day party at Mohawk, Austin, March 2019
years.h: Rough Trade signs them, and "Speedway" follows
years.p: A tour-only 12-inch with remixes by Proc Fiskal, Kwake Bass and Blanck Mass, and a video Picton made himself.

years.h: Schlagenheim arrives with its track list kept secret until release day
years.p: Rough Trade asked reviewers with early copies not to print the song titles. Metacritic: 82; Pitchfork: Best New Music.
years.xp:
The title is a word the band made up, though it has been read as German for "hit home"; several songs are set in a fictional world of the same name. David Rudnick designed the cover.

The band moved on fast. "People seemed to really like the debut album but after a while we all became pretty bored with it," Greep told the Quietus.

years.h: Release week, all four on a small stage at Rough Trade
years.p: Greep and Kwasniewski-Kelvin on guitars, Picton on bass, Simpson behind them, four days after the album came out.

years.h: The Mercury Prize shortlists Schlagenheim
years.p: black midi sit on the 2019 list alongside the 1975 and slowthai, with a debut that had entered the UK Top 50.

years.h: The band reads classic short stories over jams, Bandcamp only
years.p: The Black Midi Anthology Vol. 1: Tales of Suspense and Revenge: four stories read by band members, plus three instrumental mixes. Eleven days later they start a monthly NTS show, The Black Midi Variety Hour.

yt: Black Midi, New Road at the Windmill, early 2020
years.h: Black Midi, New Road play a £5 livestream to save the Windmill
years.p: black midi and [[Black Country, New Road|e9403d9c-329b-4108-a26f-564159d441d9]] team up under one joint name for a charity show streamed from the Windmill's Bandcamp page.
years.xp: Perry has called a Black Midi, New Road Christmas show his favourite gig ever at the venue. "Black Country, New Road are a Cambridge band, and they needed a London home and adopted us," he told the Big Issue.

eras.title: Three-piece, plus friends
eras.text: Kwasniewski-Kelvin stepped away in January 2021 and the others carried on as a trio, with Seth Evans on keys and Kaidi Akinnibi on sax filling out the sound. Two albums in fourteen months: one cut in the hills south of Dublin, one launched from an ice cream van in a heatwave.

years.src: Wikipedia: Black Midi · The Guardian · Wikipedia: Matt Kwasniewski-Kelvin
years.h: Matt Kwasniewski-Kelvin steps back for his mental health
years.p: The band says he's taking time away and won't play on new material, and that they're "fully behind our best mate in his recovery."
years.xp: He still has writing credits on a couple of Cavalcade tracks, but wasn't part of the recording. He later played on records by Greentea Peng and Wu-Lu.

yt: black midi, Performance & Interview (Live on KEXP at Home)
years.h: A second KEXP session, now with sax, keys and brass
years.p: Out the same day as the single "Slow", the at-home set has Evans, Akinnibi and a small brass section alongside the trio.

years.h: Cavalcade starts as five days in the Wicklow Mountains
years.p: The plan was a few tracks at Hellfire Studios south of Dublin with producer John "Spud" Murphy. They came back with the album.
years.xp:
"The plan was to go and record a few tracks for five days," Greep told the Quietus. They had started out working with Marta Salogni, who recorded the lead single "John L". Evans and Akinnibi play on the record, and one sound on it is a wok played with a violin bow.

Lockdown, Greep said, gave them "even more of an opportunity, individually, to further go down rabbit holes."

years.h: Back on a London festival stage as a trio
years.p: The Cavalcade lineup at Wide Awake, the first of two years of touring Europe and the US.

years.h: Support act: the Orange Tree Boys, "a funk blues band from Las Vegas"
years.p: On the 2021–22 tours the band sometimes opened for itself under that alter ego.

years.h: Covers of King Crimson, Taylor Swift and Captain Beefheart
years.p: Cavalcovers collects the covers first pressed as flexi-discs for people who pre-ordered Cavalcade on vinyl.

years.h: Greep calls Hellfire an action film after Cavalcade's drama
years.p: Thirteen days at Hoxa HQ in London with Marta Salogni. It reaches No. 22 in the UK, their best, and gives them a first US chart entry at No. 139.
years.xp:
The songs are first-person stories from flawed characters, with cabaret, country, flamenco and show tunes in the mix. "Almost everything I write is from a true thing, something I experienced and exaggerated and wrote down," Greep said.

Metacritic: 79. In 2023 it won Best Heavy Record at the A2IM Libera Awards.

years.cap: Black midi in a 2022 press photo
years.h: An ice cream van sells Hellfire around London at 40°C
years.p: Release week ran into the UK's record heatwave, 40.3°C on July 19, so the band ran an ice cream van selling merch and the album.

years.cap: Greep and Picton at Latitude Festival, Suffolk
years.h: Back in Black: a US tour with Black Country, New Road in support
years.p: The band keeps road-testing unreleased songs, among them "The Magician" and "Askance".

eras.title: "It's over"
eras.text: By 2024 the three had stopped talking much as a band, and had agreed to say nothing about it. Then Greep went live on Instagram to promote some solo shows.

q: We hadn't really been on speaking terms as a band a while before that
years.h: Greep types "no more black midi" into an Instagram Live chat
years.p: Greep called black midi "an interesting band that's now indefinitely over." Picton said he'd been blindsided; management told Pitchfork it was a hiatus for solo projects.
years.xp:
Picton on Twitter: "We'd agreed not to say anything about 'breaking up' so I was as blindsided as everyone else." A statement to the Quietus said the door was being left open.

Greep explained later that he hadn't wanted to string anyone along, and that a band can do three good years and finish: "Nothing's meant to go on forever and ever."

years.cap: Greep playing solo material at the Windmill, Brixton, March 2024
years.h: Greep's solo album The New Sound, produced by Seth Evans
years.p: Simpson drums on it, a month after he played on Nala Sinephro's Endlessness. Picton starts self-releasing mixtapes as Camera Picture.

eras.title: After the band
eras.text: The three kept working, apart. In January 2026 the band's first guitarist died at 26.

years.h: Simpson plays on Little Simz's Lotus
years.p: He's also the touring and recording drummer for the jazz musician Nala Sinephro.

years.h: Matt Kwasniewski-Kelvin dies at 26
years.p: Rough Trade shared his family's statement that he died "after a long battle with his mental health". Wikipedia records his death as a suicide.
years.xp:
His family called him "a talented musician and a kind, loving man" and asked people to check in with their loved ones. Rough Trade called him "an incredibly talented person who will be truly missed."

He played on Schlagenheim and the early singles, and on the KEXP set that introduced the band to the world.

years.h: Picton's new group My New Band Believe releases its debut
years.p: A self-titled album, with Evans as collaborator and keyboard player.
